# Preface {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-note}
## About this adaptation
This book is an adaptation of Rafael A. Irizarry's *Introduction to Data Science* (<https://rafalab.github.io/dsbook-part-2/>), created by Giorgio Arcara for the *Behavioural Data Science* course (PS0000002, University of Padua). Substantive changes — replaced datasets and case studies, new chapters, retitling — are documented in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/intro-to-behds/behdsbook-part-2/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

This work remains licensed under [CC BY-NC-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0), consistent with the original.
:::

This is the website for the **Statistics and Prediction Algorithms Through Case Studies**, the second part of **Introduction to Behavioural Data Science**, an adaptation of **Introduction to Data Science**.

This behavioural-science adaptation, *Introduction to Behavioural Data Science*, was created by Giorgio Arcara for the *Behavioural Data Science* course (PS0000002, University of Padua).

The Quarto files used to generate this adaptation are available on [GitHub](https://github.com/intro-to-behds/behdsbook-part-2).

The website for the original book are the following:

- Part 1 **Data Wrangling and Visualization with R** part is [here](https://intro-to-behds.github.io/behdsbook-part-1/).
- Part 2 **Statistics and Prediction Algorithms Through Case Studies** part is [here](https://intro-to-behds.github.io/behdsbook-part-2/).


# Disclaimers

In this version of the book, all examples and datasets are adaptations of the datasets in the original book, re-themed to fit a behavioural-science context. The numerical values derive from real datasets, but their behavioural framing is fictional: **these should not be interpreted or cited as genuine behavioural, statistical, or predictive-modeling data**.

The English translation and adaptation were produced with the assistance of _Claude Code (Sonnet 4.6)_. The model was used for programming, language revision, and to help "reflavour" the examples; LLMs were not used to generate new ideas or to decide the content.

# Preface to the Original Edition {.unnumbered}

*The following is Rafael A. Irizarry's preface to the original* Introduction to Data Science*, unchanged except where noted.*

This book started out as part of the class notes used in the HarvardX [Data Science Series](https://www.edx.org/professional-certificate/harvardx-data-science).

A hardcopy version of the first edition of the book, which combined both parts, is available from [CRC Press](https://www.routledge.com/Introduction-to-Data-Science-Data-Wrangling-and-Visualization-with-R/Irizarry/p/book/9781032116556).

A free PDF of the October 24, 2019 version of the book, which combined both parts, is available from [Leanpub](https://leanpub.com/datasciencebook).

The Quarto code used to generate the original book is available on  [GitHub](https://github.com/rafalab/dsbook-part-2).

This work is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International [CC BY-NC-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0).

We make announcements related to the book on X. For updates follow [\@rafalab](https://x.com/rafalab).

*The following are Rafael A. Irizarry's original acknowledgments, unchanged.*
